## 1. Production fix — `source/index.ts`

In the `PQueue.clear()` method, the loop currently reads exactly:

```ts
		const error = new DOMException('The queue was cleared', 'AbortError');
		for (const waitingTask of this.#waitingTasks) {
			waitingTask.stopListeningForAbort?.();
			waitingTask.isCleared = true;
			waitingTask.promise?.catch(() => undefined);
			void error; // Regression: cleared promises never settle.
		}
```

Replace the single line `void error; // Regression: cleared promises never settle.` with:

```ts
			waitingTask.reject?.(error);
```

Keep every other line exactly as-is: keep `waitingTask.stopListeningForAbort?.();`, `waitingTask.isCleared = true;`, and `waitingTask.promise?.catch(() => undefined);` (the `.catch` suppresses unhandled rejections for ignored promises). `this.#waitingTasks.clear();` must remain AFTER this loop — do not move it. Do not touch `#startNextTask`, the queued-abort listener, `#runningTasks`, or running-task cleanup. Read `source/index.ts` before editing to confirm the exact current text, then make exactly this one-line change in `clear()`.

Why: every task placed in `#waitingTasks` has its `reject` already populated (assigned before the `#waitingTasks.add(...)`), so each cleared queued `.add()` promise must now reject with `DOMException('The queue was cleared', 'AbortError')`. Currently they never settle.

## 2. New tests — `benchmark_tests/queued-cancellation.ts`

`benchmark_tests/` does not exist yet; create it. Write the new file in the same style as existing `test/basic.ts` (imports `import {test} from 'node:test';`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict';`, `import PQueue from '../source/index.js';`, single quotes, semicolons — match that file's formatting and indentation). Cover these four scenarios:

(a) `aborting the first queued item removes it and keeps stable order` — `const queue = new PQueue({autoStart: false});` add three tasks pushing into a shared `order` array and returning their label; give only the FIRST task an `AbortController` signal. Abort it before starting. Assert the first promise rejects with `{name: 'AbortError'}`; then `await queue.start(); await queue.onIdle();`; assert `order` is exactly `['second', 'third']` and the second/third promises resolve to their labels.

(b) `aborting a later queued item removes it and keeps stable order` — same three-task shape but only the SECOND task has a signal; abort it before starting. Assert its promise rejects with `{name: 'AbortError'}`, and after start/idle the order is exactly `['first', 'third']`.

(c) `clear() rejects every queued promise with AbortError and running work completes normally` — `const queue = new PQueue({concurrency: 1});` make the first task an async fn that sets a `ranFirst` flag, awaits a manually-releasable gate, and returns `'first-result'`; the second task sets a `ranSecond` flag and returns `'second'`. Add both (first starts immediately, second becomes queued). Call `queue.clear()`. Assert the second promise rejects with `{name: 'AbortError', message: 'The queue was cleared'}` and `ranSecond === false`; then release the first gate, assert the first promise resolves to `'first-result'` with `ranFirst === true`, `await queue.onIdle()` resolves `undefined`, and `queue.pending === 0`.

(d) `onPendingZero waits for running work after clear()` — same concurrency-1 running+queued shape with a releasable first gate; add both tasks, then `queue.clear()` (rejects the queued second promise). Register `const pendingZero = queue.onPendingZero().then(() => { pendingZeroResolved = true; });` with `pendingZeroResolved` initialized `false`. After a microtask flush, assert `pendingZeroResolved === false` still; then release the first gate; `await pendingZero;` and assert `pendingZeroResolved === true` and the first promise resolved to its value.

Use a small local flush helper (e.g. `const flush = async () => new Promise<void>(resolve => { setTimeout(resolve, 0); });`) where needed; keep the file self-contained (do not import from `test/`).
